title: Guaranteed throughput lexicon and degradation notice procedure
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures definitions, measurement windows, error-budget math, remedial credit language, and the operational notice procedures for Dedicated throughput guarantees. The goal is a single canonical lexicon that legal can sign off on and SRE/Eng can implement in metrics and automated billing adjustments.

Definitions we propose: 
- Committed Serve Rate (CSR): the guaranteed committed throughput expressed as tokens-per-minute (TPM) that Redwood will make available to the customer's Dedicated pool. CSR is the contract baseline.
- Measurement Anchor: CSR is measured at the cluster egress (post-queue, post-cache) aggregated across the customer's reserved pool. Measurement windows are rolling 10-minute windows for detection and a 30-day billing window for error-budget accounting.
- Degradation Minute: any 1-minute interval where aggregated observed TPM < 0.9 * CSR for that minute. We use 0.9 as a tolerance to account for sampling noise and brief scheduling jitter.
- Error Budget (EB): the allowance of Degradation Minutes per billing cycle (30 days). Default EB = ceil(0.5% * TotalMinutesInCycle). Customers and sales may negotiate alternate EB percentages.

Error budget and credit model: 
- EB accounting: count Degradation Minutes across the 30-day window. Remaining EB = EB - DegradationMinutesUsed. If Remaining EB < 0, remediation applies.
- Credit formula (simplified): Credit = min(1.0, DegradationMinutesOver / EB) * MonthlyCommittedFee * CreditFactor. CreditFactor defaults to 0.5 (i.e., customers may receive up to 50% of the proportional monthly fee back for severe degradations).
- Example: MonthlyCommittedFee = $20,000, EB = 216 minutes (0.5% of 30-day minutes). If DegradationMinutesUsed = 432 (double EB), DegradationMinutesOver = 216 -> Credit = (216/216)*20000*0.5 = $10,000 credited to customer's account.

Autoscale and fallback interplay: 
- Autoscaler policies (ENG-managed) have two axes: throughput-driven (queue length and request arrival rate) and utilization-driven (GPU / vCPU). Autoscale behavior that temporarily reduces per-customer effective throughput due to rapid scaledown will not count as SLA breach if: (a) the request was placed into a configured burst queue and served within the customer's CSR latency SLO, or (b) autoscale events are part of a documented maintenance window.
- Model variant fallback: automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant (e.g., quantized or distilled) triggered by capacity pressure is considered a remediation measure. Fallback usage does NOT count as a breach provided the fallback path is transparent to the customer (logged and surfaced in the Console) and the customer has opted into the fallback policy. If fallback is used without prior opt-in, minutes served on fallback count as Degradation Minutes unless the fallback meets at least 95% of CSR.

Notice, escalation, and remediation procedures: 
- Scheduled maintenance: Redwood will provide at least 60 minutes' notice for non-critical maintenance that affects Dedicated serving. For planned capacity reconfiguration (reservations, AZ changes) Redwood will provide 24-hour notice and an opt-out window for large customers.
- Incident notification: For incidents that may impact CSR we will: create an incident in the Console, send an initial customer notification (within 15 minutes of detection for P0/P1), and open a remediation plan.
- Credits and reconciliation: After incident closure and metric validation, legal/billing will compute credits using the formula above and issue credit within the next billing cycle. Disputed measurements trigger a reconciliation SLA (30 days to resolve) with supporting metrics exported to the customer on request.

Implementation and observability requirements: 
- Metric hooks: Add and publish the following Prometheus metrics: dedicated_csr_committed_tpm, dedicated_csr_observed_tpm, dedicated_degradation_minutes_total (counter), dedicated_eb_allowed_minutes (gauge). Metric names and label schemas are in the attached metrics spec doc.
- Dashboards: Console must show percent-of-CSR over 5m and 10m windows, plus EB consumption graph over rolling 30 days.
- Audit trail: All autoscale/fallback events affecting Dedicated pool must be logged with timestamps, triggers, and affected model variants. Logs must be exportable for reconciliation.

Legal phrasing suggestions (high level for negotiation): 
- Define CSR as 'Committed Serve Rate measured at the customer-reserved pool egress averaged on rolling 10-minute windows over the calendar month unless otherwise agreed.'
- Define Credit cap as 'Credits issued in respect of failures to meet CSR shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of the monthly committed fee for the affected Dedicated pool for the billing cycle.'
- Include a 'grace allowance' clause for force majeure, cloud provider network partition, or customer-side misconfiguration.

Open decisions / trade-offs: 
1) Tolerance threshold: Use 0.9 * CSR per-minute vs 0.95. 0.9 reduces false positives but allows slightly larger dips; 0.95 is stricter but risks noisy credit churn. PM recommends 0.9 for initial launch.
2) EB percentage: Default 0.5% of minutes per 30-day cycle vs 0.25% (stricter) or 1% (more permissive). We propose 0.5% as balance.
3) Whether fallback counts toward breach: default opt-in required. This reduces disputes at scale.

Acceptance criteria (listed separately below) outline the codeland, legal, and console changes required before sign-off.

Artifacts and links:
- Metrics / implementation spec (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Committed+Serve+Rate+Spec
- Draft legal annex (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-rr-example-legal-draft
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7321
- Console wireframes: https://www.figma.com/file/example/dedicated-csr-console

Longer-term notes: Consider an SLI tiering approach where CSR can be expressed as a small percentile band (e.g., 50th/95th within a corridor) for customers who want banded guarantees rather than a single threshold. This doc focuses on a single-threshold model because it is simpler to implement and bill against initially.
acceptance_criteria: Prometheus metrics exist and exported (committed_tpm, observed_tpm, degradation_minutes_total, eb_allowed_minutes)
Console dashboard shows rolling 5m/10m CSR utilization and 30-day EB burn with export capability
Billing pipeline calculates credits per the formula and a test dataset demonstrates correct credit issuance
Legal approves the draft annex wording and credit cap language
SRE/ENG implement autoscale/fallback logging and document the opt-in policy in the Console settings
QA run with synthetic traffic validates Degradation Minutes detection and credit computation with end-to-end tests
